title: What breaks it
hookLine: eating, drinking, intimacy from dawn to sunset; forgetting doesn't break it (Bukhari)

lines: THE OFFICE KITCHEN. A GLASS OF WATER.
cards: A fasting day, the office kitchen, a full glass of water, and a hand already lifting it halfway before the brain catches up. Or worse: a few swallows gone before anyone remembers. Panic.
Is the whole day lost? Do you start over tomorrow, or owe something? The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ was asked about exactly this, and his answer is gentle.
But first, the rules it softens. Today, what breaks the fast, and what doesn't.

teach.b: First, the frame, from surah two.

The fasting believer is told, in Pickthall's words, to "eat and drink until the white thread becometh distinct to you from the black thread of the dawn. Then strictly observe the fast till nightfall."
The same verse permits marital intimacy in the nights of the fast. So the day runs from the first thread of dawn to sunset, and in those hours the fast is broken by eating, drinking and intimacy.
The legal books add details, like deliberately vomiting, and the schools discuss newer questions, but those three are the core. Second, the word that matters is deliberately.

In Sahih al-Bukhari, the Prophet ﷺ said that if someone fasting forgets and eats or drinks, they should complete their fast, because it was Allah who fed them and gave them drink. Not a failure: a meal from Allah.
The fast simply continues. Third, what that answer does. The fast is strict about the clock; dawn means dawn.
Yet the person who honestly forgot hasn't broken anything, and yesterday's intention holds.

teach.h: A WILL, NOT A PERFECT MEMORY.
teach.b: The fast asks for a will, not a flawless memory.

teach.h: THIS WEEK: GIVING, THEN THE FAST.
teach.b: Fourth, this week in one breath: the eight doors of zakat, khums in Shia law, giving with dignity, zakat and sadaqah, the many hands, then the turn into the fast, an intention in the heart, and today, rules with mercy built in.

teach.h: THEN STRICTLY OBSERVE THE FAST TILL NIGHTFALL.
teach.b: And it reaches past the fast: a slip is not the same as a choice.

how: Muslims who are fasting abstain from food, drink and marital intimacy from dawn until sunset; someone who eats or drinks by honest mistake carries on fasting, following the report in Sahih al-Bukhari.

o: any food or drink at all, even when you honestly forgot
missing the pre-dawn meal before the fast begins at dawn
eating, drinking or intimacy on purpose between dawn and sunset

games.q: what breaks it — tap the pairs.

s: if you forget and drink while fasting, the day is lost
the report in Bukhari says finish the fast: Allah fed you and gave you drink.
the Qur'an sets the fast from the first thread of dawn until nightfall
surah 2:187: eat and drink until the white thread is distinct from the black, then fast till nightfall.
the nights of Ramadan are under the same rules as the days
the same verse permits eating, drinking and marital intimacy in the nights.

games.q: you're fasting, and you've just realized you drank a glass of water without thinking. what does the report in Bukhari say?
o: stop fasting; the day is broken.
complete the fast; Allah fed you and gave you drink.
fast an extra day to make up for it.
games.why: complete the fast. the one who forgot hasn't broken it; the food and drink are counted as a gift from Allah.

practice: Bring to mind a recent slip, small and honest: a promise you forgot, a habit you meant to keep, a word out before you thought. Not something you chose; something that got past you.
Look at it plainly, then set it down the way the report sets down the forgotten glass of water, and if you pray, hand it to Allah.

wordCard.voice: What breaks it. Eating, drinking and intimacy, on purpose, between dawn and sunset. Forgetting doesn't: the one who forgot finishes the fast. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: he forgot; the word at the heart of the report about eating while fasting.

carryVoice: Your line: forgetting is Allah's gift. The fast goes on, and so does the day. A week, done.
